evals.prompt: I'm about to commit code that handles user auth and HTML templates. Check for security pitfalls.
evals.expected_output: Guardrails triggers, lists Anti-example 2 (secret & credential hygiene) and Anti-example 1 (HTML/DOM sink escaping, canvas morph protection, and explicit event bindings), showing .gitignore deny-list and runtime secret injection rather than committing .env.
assertions: Correct .gitignore deny-list and HTML sink escaping pattern shown

evals.prompt: I need to harden our Dockerfile and dependency manifest for a production release.
evals.expected_output: Guardrails triggers, shows Anti-example 3: single-stage root container with build toolchains vs multi-stage build with locked manifest targeting a minimal non-root distroless runtime image.
assertions: Guardrails triggered on container and dependency hardening query
Contrast table includes multi-stage locked build and non-root distroless runtime
Why explains least-privilege execution and removing build toolchains from production images

evals.prompt: Review my Rust code that checks if user is null and handles lifetimes.
evals.expected_output: Guardrails triggers, shows Anti-examples 4 (null vs Option) and 5 (lifetime elision) with before/after Rust snippets.
assertions: Anti-example 4: null vs Option shown with if let Some

evals.prompt: I'm just exploring the codebase, reading the README without modifying anything.
evals.expected_output: Guardrails does NOT trigger — only reading, no code touching deps/Docker/HTML/auth. Suggest explore mode, no guardrails load.
assertions: Guardrails did NOT trigger on read-only prompt
